history.summary: The Old Somnath Temple stands opposite the present Somnath Jyotirlinga Temple at Prabhas Patan. After Aurangzeb ordered the destruction of the main shrine in 1706, worship had no safe home; Maratha queen Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore built this smaller temple around 1783 CE (sources variously say 1783/1785/1786) so pilgrims could continue worshipping Lord Shiva near the original site. Local tradition holds that the swayambhulinga's location came to her in a dream, and many devotees believe the original Jyotirlinga was hidden here for safekeeping. Unlike the new temple, devotees may enter its garbhagriha and perform abhishek with the local priest; its Shivling sits below ground level. It served as the primary place of worship at Somnath until the 20th-century reconstruction of the main temple. Coordinates are those of the adjacent main Somnath Temple; the Ahilyabai temple stands directly opposite it, so coordinates are approximate. RELATED to seq 1514 (Somnath Jyotirlinga Temple), which is the adjacent modern main shrine - this is the separate, older Ahilyabai structure, not a duplicate.

name: Somnath Mahadev Temple (Ahilyabai Temple)
town_description: Somnath, at Prabhas Patan in Gir Somnath district, is one of the most sacred towns in Hinduism as the home of the first of the twelve Jyotirlingas. Set on the Arabian Sea coast in Gujarat's Saurashtra region, it is a major pilgrimage centre alongside its temples, the Triveni Ghat, and a growing beachside tourism belt.
